title: Grain boundary engineered aluminum current collector for energy-dense initially anode-free sodium metal batteries
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 06 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74177-8

The initially anode-free sodium metal offer advantages in energy density and safety. Here, authors design a grain-boundary Ga-rich polycrystalline aluminum current collector that enables controlled Al3+ dissolution to compensate Na loss, stabilizes Na plating/stripping, and delivers reversible batteries.

title: Cryo-EM structures of heteromeric Kir4.1/5.1 channel suggest mechanisms of inward rectification and channel blockage
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 06 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74087-9

Kir4.1/5.1 channels are vital for brain and kidney function. Here the authors combine structural, electrophysiological, and computational studies to reveal an inner-ring pore blockage mechanism by polyamines and inhibitors, providing the structural basis for inward rectification.

title: Mapping the absorption landscape of far-red Photosystem II
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 06 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-73964-7

Some cyanobacteria do oxygenic photosynthesis with near-infrared photons using specialized pigments. Here, the authors identify their positions and colors by combining phylogenetic, spectroscopic, and structural methods.

title: ArchVelo: archetypal velocity modeling for single-cell multi-omic trajectories
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 06 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74000-4

Mapping cell dynamics from static data is a challenge in genomics. Here, authors introduce ArchVelo, a computational method for modeling transcription dynamics and trajectory inference using chromatin accessibility archetypes in single-cell multi-omics, and infer new T cell transitions in infection.

title: Bioinspired nano-architecture for cellulose fibers with spider silk–like toughness
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 06 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74052-6

Cellulose fibers derived from renewable biomass offer great tensile strength performance, but their toughness remains limited. Here the authors develop cellulose fibers with uniquely high toughness and tensile strength, that can form from single fibers to woven fabrics.

title: Neuroligin1 in CCK-interneurons gates social memory formation via a disinhibitory microcircuit in the hippocampal CA2 in male mice
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 06 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-73903-6

In this study, the authors present that cholecystokinin-positive interneurons (CCK-INs) in hippocampal dorsal CA2 are essential for social memory encoding in male mice by mediating disinhibition of pyramidal neurons. Deficiency of Neuroligin 1 disrupts CCK-INs activity and induces social memory impairments, offering potential therapeutic targets for related psychiatric disorders.

title: Indium-Based Octahedra Coordinating Pb–I Termini for Stable Perovskites
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 06 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74107-8

Halide perovskites degrade at surfaces where defects break octahedral connectivity and destabilize the structure. Wen et al. design indium-based octahedral compounds that bind lead-iodide, forming rigid interfaces that enhance stability and carrier transport for efficient, durable solar cells.

title: Post-polyploid chromosomal diploidization in plants is affected by clade divergence and constrained by shared genomic features
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 06 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-73793-8

Flowering plants can undergo whole-genome duplications, but how they return to diploid-like states is poorly understood. Here authors show diploidization in the Biscutella genus is shaped by clade divergence and constrained by shared genomic features.
